$comment: Canonical-bytes worked example. Inputs and expected sha256 / signature bytes come from rs/crates/sign/examples/gen-fixture.rs. The signature was produced with the fixture's ephemeral private key seed; a conformant implementation reaches the SAME canonical bytes (sha256 matches) and the SAME signature (Ed25519 is deterministic per RFC 8032).

shared.$comment_seed: Test fixture only — not a real key. 32-byte raw seed; load into Ed25519 via RFC 8032 §5.1.5.

vectors.name: sample_envelope
vectors.description: Primary canonical-bytes vector. ts is in the middle of the cert validity window (1700000000..2524607999), so a clock-skew check at nowMs == ts passes.

vectors.name: near_not_before_envelope
vectors.description: Signed at (not_before + 5s). nowMs slightly before not_before passes clock-skew (|skew|<60s) but fails the cert validity-window check.

vectors.name: near_not_after_envelope
vectors.description: Signed at (not_after - 5s). nowMs slightly past not_after passes clock-skew but fails validity-window.

vectors.name: get_disclosure_empty_body
vectors.description: GET disclosure request canonical bytes — body is the empty string, NOT omitted. The trailing LF before the (empty) body is required.
vectors.$comment: Implementations that strip the trailing LF will compute a different digest and fail to verify. The format is `method LF url LF ts LF nonce LF body`; when body is empty, the last byte before EOF is the LF that separates nonce from body.
